answer: To prevent Sybil identities, optical retroreflection anchors each agent to verified physical coordinates. Nodes authenticate by aiming a steering mirror to return pulsed laser beacons to base stations across a river or wild yarrow field. Forging extra identities forces an attacker to deploy separate optical gimbals and physical mounts, imposing substantial capital costs per persona. However, dense fog or heavy precipitation attenuates the beam, causing intermittent authentication dropouts.
